title: SignWriting developer tools
sourcePolicy: Curated from maintainer documentation and package registries. Versions are reviewed snapshots; source and research projects have their own release and maintenance status.

groups.title: JavaScript
groups.subtitle: Browser and Node.js
groups.description: Start with core for text processing. Choose font-ttf for browser rendering or font-db for Node.js, then add components or an editor.

groups.title: PHP
groups.subtitle: Server-side text processing
groups.description: Use the Composer library for the FSW/SWU text model in PHP applications.

groups.title: Python
groups.subtitle: Text, rendering, and data workflows
groups.description: Use the Sutton packages for core text operations and font rendering. For external NLP and research libraries, continue to the next section.

groups.title: External libraries & processing tools
groups.subtitle: Community software and research
groups.description: Find structured-data, tokenization, evaluation, font-building, and annotation tools maintained outside sutton-signwriting. Each card identifies its owner and environment.

tools.name: Core
tools.summary: Parse and validate FSW/SWU text, convert representations, and work with queries and style strings.

tools.name: Font TTF
tools.summary: Render symbols, signs, and structured text as SVG or PNG using the TrueType fonts.

tools.name: Font database
tools.summary: Render symbols, signs, and structured text from the SQLite symbol database, including command-line workflows.

tools.name: Web components
tools.summary: Use reusable SignWriting components in browser interfaces.

tools.name: SignMaker
tools.summary: Write and edit FSW/SWU signs in the existing editor, or embed it in your own application.

tools.name: Core for PHP
tools.summary: Parse and convert FSW/SWU, build queries, and handle style strings in PHP.
tools.requirements: Requires mbstring. The package declares PHP ^7.3 or ^8.0 compatibility.

tools.name: Core for Python
tools.summary: Process FSW/SWU text, queries, conversions, and style strings in Python.

tools.name: Font rendering for Python
tools.summary: Compose SVG and PNG output for symbols, signs, and text using the SQLite symbol database.

tools.name: SignWriting utilities
tools.summary: Parse FSW into structured objects, tokenize text for NLP, convert formats, and generate images.
tools.note: The repository documents the current installation. Its visualizer has different styling support from font-db.

tools.name: SignWriting evaluation
tools.summary: Compare machine-generated SignWriting with token, character, image, and symbol-distance metrics.
tools.note: Metric scores answer specific comparison questions; they do not by themselves establish writing quality.

tools.name: Complex tokenization
tools.summary: Explore tokenization methods for complex scripts and language-specific structural decompositions.

tools.name: SignWriting font tools
tools.summary: Inspect and rebuild external OneD and TwoD font work from the documented source pipeline.
tools.note: These builds have their own implementation and review history, separate from the published Sutton font packages.

tools.name: SignWriting Annotator
tools.summary: Explore a browser annotation project for relating signed-language videos to written signs.

communityExtension.name: ssw-ext
communityExtension.summary: Community experiments with symbol properties, mirroring and sign transformations, descriptions, and temporal sequencing.
communityExtension.currentImplementation: Prototypes extend the FSW functions in font-ttf and depend on core. Proposed functions have different levels of maturity.
communityExtension.integrationStatus: The GitHub maintainer response recommends continued standalone development. Inclusion in core, font-ttf, or font-db has not been accepted.
communityExtension.reviewBoundary: A hand symbol alone does not deterministically identify the left or right hand. Handedness assumptions, description wording, and temporal ordering need domain review.

possiblePackageReview.scope: Representation-level utilities, only where their meaning can be specified and verified without font rendering.
Browser rendering or display helpers, evaluated against the published font-based behavior.
Applicable server-rendering counterparts after shared behavior is established and parity is tested.
